As i have said a 100 times: the crust is the thing. It can make or break any pizza joint and this place is a pizza joint with several pizzas, drinks (not at the point alcoholic...take a flask). In all ways this makes it harder for management to keep focus: fewer products, mainly in this case Pizzas: all about said pizzas must be perfect because you have little to take the focus away from your main offering. The crust: in many ways this crust reminds me of that of the Luggage Room in Pasadena though it has it own particular flavor and character derived from a venue that began in NYC. Revolver is firmly ensconced on St Andres near the Foodland and not at all in any area that attracts much foot traffic or needy so called Millenials. But they will find their way here. They always do. And this will be good for the Revolver and for the Westside. So the product: White Pizza with Veggies Pizza Rosso As i said the crust is thick-ish but not to. The veggies on the White pizza were a mix of ricotta, onions, broccoli rabe, sauteed onions, green onions from what i remember though i would think the veg changes with the seasons. But a non red sauce pizza that the kiddoes would eat without whining is a primo pizza to me. we adults loved it because there was so much care as to veg selection and preparation. Each taste was jam packed with flavor. even the onions were sweet from a long saute with salt, pepper and maybe a bit of sugar. On the face of it a "White Pizza" sounds boring so the Rev folks knew what had to be done: make each element as flavorful and savory as they could within the limitations of the ingredients themselves. In other words: prep, cook, roast each one and make each element sing. The Rosso pizza on the same delectable crust was closer to what we usually order and the use of excellent italian tomatoes and first rate cheese selection as well as oregano leaf and basil make this a very special pie. There are a few more pizzas to order and i will get to all of them. Plus my guess is that Revolver will run specials as per what is available from all of the product and meats available in the Central Coast. Bravo to Revolver! Welcome to the neighborhood.

text: Two stars for a beautiful venue and good oysters. Company holiday dinner, eight of us, in a small room in the upstairs of the restaurant. - Decent enough wine list, albeit extremely basic and non inspiring . - We joined three of our group that were already seated and enjoying a beverage, and waited about fifteen minutes to be approached by our server and offered a drink. - This is the last thing I will review regarding the service, so I could get to the food...our server was a nice guy but his service was, considering the venue and reputation it has, completely unprofessional and unknowledgeable. No mignonette or anything else remotely upscale or different . - Stuffed mushrooms were served at almost room temperature. Very thick cream sauce with them. Came to me medium plus, and room temperature. The steak was not setting all that time, just not picked up before it continued to cook past my desired temperature and lose all of its heat. Not good and very disappointing. - Shrimp risotto. Thick, globby cream. Not the creaminess of a proper risotto, but so much thick roux and cream I couldn't even tell it was risotto. text: We were driving from Tampa to Lakewood Ranch on the i-75 and needed a non fast food option for lunch. We saw the mostly positive Yelp reviews for this place and decided to give it a go. The building is a stand-alone roadside eatery beckoning you in with flashing lights promising soups, sandwiches, and the best pies. The interior reminded me of an old school DQ with red moulded plywood booths, neon lighting and large over-counter menu. You can do dine in or take out. There is a self serve fountain drink area. The bathroom is hard to find despite the handmade sign directing you to it. (although a very helpful employee guided me -- clearly i was looking lost) You basically have to walk into their kitchen and the bathroom doubles as their furnace and supply closet. An employee was dividing up a cake in the hallway to the bathroom as I went by. Not a great first impression. The menu offerings are also extensive (which to me is always a sign of danger...it's impossible to do that many things well). Under the counter is a massive dessert case featuring pies, bars, cakes and cookies. All look fantastic. We ordered a tomato sandwich ($6), a chicken salad sandwich ($8), chicken noodle soup ($4) and a Reuben ($8). And cannolis and a napoleon for dessert. Positives: the bread was very fresh on all our sandwiches. The soup had interesting ingredients (zucchini). Portions are large. Sandwiches are the size of a small dinner plate and stuffed thick with whatever inside you ordered. Not so positive: all sandwiches were severely lacking in seasoning. Tomato and chicken salad sandwiches had lots of mayo, zero salt or pepper. Reuben was a bit more successful because of the cheese, sauerkraut and thousand island dressing. Oddly the chicken noodle soup was very very salty. And the noodles were crushed spaghetti which I find hard to tackle with a small plastic spoon. Not a deal breaker, but a peccadillo. Desserts were a disappointment too. Cannolis had a nice cream. Napoleon tasted frozen. Not surprised if they were as it would be hard to keep the amount of choices they had fresh. Good concept, but I would prefer a shortened sandwich menu done well and a few fresh favourite desserts instead of trying to have something for everyone.

text: If you are a military family and looking for a dental office in the St. Louis area, look no further. We are an Army family and trying to look for a dental office which accepts Tricare, let alone understand the process, is cumbersome. So being recently transferred here, we thought we would bite the bullet and try the closest dental office to our home, and we really lucked out with finding The Dental Center. It doesn't seem like much from the outside, just a red sign in the middle of strip mall, but upon entering the office, you walk into a upscale lobby-definitely not your typical dental office. The office was clean and inviting. I was pretty impressed considering the outside appearance of the building. The staff promptly greeted me and were extremely helpful. They sat me down and guided me through their online process for new clients. I never felt rushed or talked down upon. I was quickly ushered to the back x-ray area by Kate who went ahead and started my x-rays. She had heard that we were new patients and asked if I had recent x-rays in the past year with the same insurance. I stated yes she consulted with the front office staff regarding double charging insurance. The decision was made to forgo the full x-rays so we wouldn't have to pay out of pocket. That was a great catch on Kate's part, as most dental offices would just go ahead with the x-rays and charge the patient if the insurance wouldn't pay out. My dental hygienist was Kristy and she was very sweet. She went over my dental history and addressed all my concerns in a very polite and professional manner. My cleaning went smoothly and efficiently. I stated I felt like I needed braces and she did a quick 10 minute online application for me (including photos) of my teeth to the Invisaline company to see if I was a candidate. And the best part was that I didn't feel pressured to purchase any additional procedures. Next up was the dental exam by Dr. Christopher Hawkins. Dr. Hawkins, I quickly found out, is also a dentist with the Missouri National Guard. Upon learning that my husband is also an AGR Guardsman, he stated that my husband should bring in a certain blank dental form for his visit the next week to expedite his next military medical screenings. Dr. Hawkins would sign off on the form while in the dental office so my husband would save time during the SRP process. This is definitely an above and beyond moment gesture which my husband and myself appreciate. Having someone who understands how burdensome the military process is, but yet still chooses to go the extra mile to assist military families is someone who deserves to get recognized. My first dental experience with this office was fantastic and I intend on telling all our military friends of the great service we received here.

I ain't pass the bar but I know a little bit and it's somebody's law that anything that can go wrong, will, and it really did. I can deal with the normal things you may experience living in an apartment building -- you know, a false fire alarm here and there, loud music, somebody blowing loud on your floor. Apparently an apartment above mine flooded and wreaked havoc that The Ave had no idea/no intention to fix properly. While the clear answer was to move all effected tenants to different apartments while they made repairs, they chose to try to work around us. My God, this experience was hell. They didn't really respond for a week and when they did, they sent workers that knew nothing about repairing flood damage. They were in and out the apartment for over a month...do you know how much of a headache that is, especially when you work from home? And in the end, they didn't really fix much...SOOO not only did we have to deal with the immediate damage of the flood but then went on to have mold for the rest of our stay at The Ave. But don't worry, they told me that it wasn't actually mold. Going back to my advice to you. When I said, "Save your life" -- I meant it quite literally -- as in there was a shootout at The Ave during my time there. text: This place is totally my style -- good ingredients treated nicely with a great deal of creativity; swanky upscale setting; unique cocktails; impeccable service. I would happily settle here for a long night with friends, drinks, and clever nibbles, (over)indulging. Chips & salsa: Fresh fresh fresh, crispy crunchy, excellent salsa. (And I grew up in Southern California, so I am fussy about my salsa.) Too good to waste -- I took the uneaten chips home. Spicy bloody Maria: Not quite spicy enough for me, but I loved the fresh jalapeño, which I ate with gusto. Guacamole: ALMOST as good as mine (which I've been making since my teens, several decades, now). Practically licked the bowl. Mex'Orean Fried Chicken Buns: Odd. Just kind of a plain-tasting fried chicken slider. Pickled cucumber slices were so thin and few I didn't taste them. Good crunchy crust, but I'll pass in the future. (I wish I'd tried their mac 'n' cheese, which looks awesome.) Tacos: Simple, not overdone. Could use more fillings, served with the traditional double-tortilla. The al Pastor was different than I'm used to -- little fried pork bits, rather than savory slow-cooked pulled pork. Two of them were not filling, but the idea is to get a round, have a drink, chat, then get another round... pull up a chair and stay a while. Some of the offerings were creative... but my kingdom for a proper taco de lengua! Chili-glazed potatoes: The sticky-sweetness of the glaze was... well, too sweet. There wasn't enough salt or chili. Mexican Poutine: Having just moved from Canada... well, His Goatness kinda had to get this. Wish I had, too. Wonderful melding of flavors and made a great brunch. Service: Flawless. I believe our server's name was Andrew... he was really on point. The joint is pricey, but is totally worth hanging out in for a long afternoon.

text: Last night we made a dinner reservation for 4 at The Library, being that we had never been there before and didn't know how busy they would be. Upon arrival we were told by the hostess that there was absolutely no availability inside and we could only sit outside. Mind you the restaurant at this time (7PM on a Saturday night) was maybe 1/2 full. There were more open tables than there were filled tables. We obviously were not thrilled but we wanted to remain optimistic and took a table outside. Had it not been so windy it would have been perfect outdoor dining weather, however it was super windy and as the sun set, it was pretty cold. We asked the server if they could turn on the heat lamps and she said that they don't work. Great. After our drink order was placed, about 15 minutes later another server came outside to tell us that the other server had left for the night and that she would be taking over. She suggested we move inside since it was so windy and cold, and we told her that the hostess had told us that there were no tables available. She looked utterly confused. Finally we are able to move inside to one of the empty tables. So at this point you are probably thinking, why didn't you just leave, this place sounds awful?? Well, we really wanted to give it a chance, and I'm glad we did. The interior of the restaurant is an architectural dream! Intricate chevron wood floors, tall book cases filled with an array of blue books, and framed artwork. The design and ambiance is beautiful and definitely picture worthy. Our second server (Brooke) who we had for the remainder of the evening was incredible. She was super bubbly and fun, and she definitely turned the night around for us. We started with Prosecco and Cucumber Collins, Pinot Grigio and a Yingling. The drinks were all wonderful and exactly as to be expected. Now to the food! For appetizers we ordered Burrata, Fried Brussel Sprouts, and the Hand Cut Beef Tartare. Upon arrival the Burrata was more like melted mozzarella with tomato sauce, it was good but not great. However, the fried brussel sprouts more than made up for it. They were sooooo incredibly delicious. Outside fried and crispy, inside nice and hot, but soft and flavorful. Served with lemon wedge and a garlic aioli that was the perfect pairing. I thought I was in heaven until the Beef Tartare arrived. Mind you, I hate beef tartare normally. I think at most places it's bland and nothing special. I wanted to try it though and I've never been happier. It was the best thing I had all night! It was so divine we ordered a second round! It was amazing and definitely a MUST try. The flavor combination was out of this world. Finally on to the entrees we ordered the Branzino, Spaghetti Bolognese, Filet Mignon, and New York Strip. The Branzino was cooked to perfection and full of flavor, however the broclininand couscous seemed bland, definitely expected more from the sides with this dish. Spaghetti Bolognese was delicious, and the pasta was cooked just the way I like it. The New York Strip was cooked perfectly, and the grilled onion complemented it nicely. The creamy mashed potatoes were incredible, and personally I wished they came with my filet mignon too. The filet was incredible and was so juicy and soft my knife cut through it like butter. The asparagus and potatoes were great, and full of interesting spices. However compared to the creamy mashed potatoes I was just left wanting something more. I think since the filet itself was so juicy and tender I wanted a soft potato to pair with it. But that could just be me. After all of this we were too full for dessert, but next time we will definitely save room to try them. Overall it was a good dining experience. We hope that next time we will be greeted better and have a smoother seating experience, but the food was great!

text: Let me start this review by saying that Jeff Ruby's steakhouse is an upscale dining restaurant. With that said, suite coat attire is not necessary but you will see some patrons wearing them. I was unsure leading up to my dining experience so I wore one. There were also patrons wearing nice jeans and button up shirts. I would not wear less than that for you may feel inadequately dressed. Now I'll begin my review. Tonight's dinner in Nashville was highly hyped up. And it delivered in full. Jeff Ruby's from its appetizers to dessert were exceptional. The complementary bread with their truffle butter was unique but delicious. Next we had a sushi appetizer, the music city roll. The fish was fresh and the combined ingredients caused an explosion of flavor. Lastly for appetizers, the wedge salad that we split was HUGE, the bacon was extra thick and the blue cheese dressing was abundant. For our main entree we split the 24oz porterhouse. The steak was cooked to a mouth watering perfect medium rare. The staff was nice enough to split it in the back so we could easily enjoy the steak. The steak was still oozing juice when served table side. The seasoning used with the steak was exceptional. Truly cooked and seasoned to perfection where no condiment were needed to aid in flavor. The two sides that we chose were the Mack and cheese and the Nashville hot greens. Both were delicious, the Mac and cheese was exceptional. The Nashville greens have a bit of heat which make you go back for more. Lastly, my wife's favorite part of the meal, the desert. It was the well known and huge Jack Daniels chocolate truffle cake. It was exceptionally moist with a light hint of Jack Daniels. Nothing to deter from, it was extremely mild and had a unique taste. So far, on this first visit to Nashville I can say confidently that this has been our favorite place to dine! I would also recommend reservations as this place gets really busy!

text: It's difficult to put into words what's been so frustrating about Hello Donuts so far - a place that is very local to where I live, and should be a welcome addition to the neighborhood, but I'll try to just go in order of the things that frustrate me every time I stop by. 1. Fillings for donuts are far, far too wet. When you have a Nutella filled donut that you're enthusiastically advertising on your Instagram, thoughts of that thick, pleasantly creamy Nutella texture take over and one expects the donut to live up to them - instead, it's akin to trying to eat soup out of a bread bowl that you're holding in your hand in your car on your way to work. 2. The service is not particularly engaged, considering how infrequently the place is busy when I've come in. Asking for a coffee with "no room" is immediately understood in Reanimator, because they ask you every time otherwise whether you want room for cream and sugar. At Hello, they'll just assume you want an 80% filled cup of coffee, then walk away immediately. I don't need to be fawned over by any stretch of the imagination, but some level of engagement with the coffee part of the business would be greatly appreciated. 3. The amount of vegan options are commendable, but sometimes flavors that would simply taste better with dairy (chocolate covered donuts particularly) are always vegan, and always suffer as a result. 4. I realize that if people aren't knocking down the doors, it's tough to offer fresh, warm donuts - but considering the condition of some by the time it's later in the day, rotating them would be something that would keep people who aren't early risers more satisfied with the offerings. The knock on Hello before they had a brick and mortar was that by the time donuts were delivered to outposts, they weren't particularly fresh tasting any longer - and it's a shame to see that happening with the location of the baking process itself. There are good things though! There's the shell of a very nice little coffee shop. But when you're a couple of blocks from Reanimator, which partially owns Hello if I understand correctly, there's very little reason to go to Hello unless you just badly need a donut. I'm always just left wishing I'd gone to Reanimator and traded a pretty good yeast donut (something that this city still lacks, since Federal just makes incredibly dry and crumbly cake donuts that are the most overrated donuts perhaps in the whole country) for an excellent all-around experience. I think Hello will still potentially get there, and I'll update this review if they do.

text: I last wrote a review of something special five years ago so it's time for an update! The Good News: They now like me (ish). If you are looking for salads, you better be thinking 'southern salads' of coleslaw, chicken salad and fruit salad cuz they won't be giving you a garden salad. The winter veggies are spot on with brussel sprouts in balsamic, twice baked potatoes and french green beans being winners IME. I like that they have normal human size portions. As a feminist, I'm not going to expect a big smile but maybe a 'hello' would be a good way to let people know that you appreciate your business? This isn't a glitch. It's a constant of my experiences there. It was only with COVID that I appreciated the hilarity of the grumpsters in charge. text: New spot taking over the old Uno that's been vacant for years. For less than $30 a person, you get all you care to eat hot pot and bbq. The center grill is also electric which cooks adequately but not quite the full charcoal flavor. On the upside the vents are built in and we didn't walk out smelling too bad. The place is very loud with hard surfaces reflecting sound and on top of that there's a loud k pop soundtrack. Fine for a small booth but wouldn't call it a place for dinner and conversation. I did see larger tables that can fit about 10 as well. Selection of meats, seafood, and vegetables was adequate and overall tasty. Stick with the unseasoned cuts, the bulgogi was overly sweet and underwhelming. But the pork belly and prime rib were delicious. text: Decided to try out this place on south street a few weeks ago for a birthday dinner. It looks pretty assuming from the outside, but the menu posted by the door was really appealing (plenty of vegetarian options!), so I decided to give it a try. Our waiter was super helpful from the get-go, suggesting the number of dishes (small plates) and order of dishes to have a satisfying meal. We decided on 6 dishes total, including the chilled potato and cucumber soup, savory donuts, Japanese eggplant, king oyster mushroom, enoki mushrooms, and grilled turbo. Soup: really really good. Lots of cucumber flavor, and a wonderful creamy texture. Savory donuts: okay. Good umami flavor but too dry for me, since I didn't eat the accompanying whitefish dip. I heard that the dip was great though. Japanese eggplant: maybe my favorite dish of the meal. The eggplant was beautifully soft and sweet/sour/spicy. It was covered with fresh cucumbers, a feta foam, and crunchy pistachios that tied King oyster mushroom: okay. Nothing that stuck out in my mind after a few weeks. Enoki mushrooms: also delicious! Tasted like cacio e Pepe, but with mushrooms in lieu of pasta. It came in a savory, cheesy broth. As a birthday bonus, we also got chocolate truffles with a side of sunflower milk. It was the perfect end to the meal--small bites of dense chocolate that didn't leave us too full. All in all, the meal was really good! Everything was aesthetically pleasing and flavorful. I was happy with the amount of vegetarian dishes they had (although none were main dishes). The meal also took really long, since there were long pauses between the courses. The waiter and staff were apologetic for the delay, but I still had the dock a star because of the inconvenience.

text: Nice, casual, simple old-school-St. Louis Italian restaurant that you don't have to go to the Hill neighborhood for. If you want something else, then go somewhere else. But if this is what you want, then you've found it here. The Rich & Charlie's salad is a classic. It has iceberg lettuce, pimentos, red onion, artichokes, parmesan cheese, and has been tossed in dressing. Generally it is made beforehand, so the lettuce is slightly soggy. This is by design. So you either like it or not - but most St. Louisans know that this is their style. Splurge the extra $1.50 for Provel cheese on top, which comes grated, rather than extruded. A small difference from some other restaurants, perhaps, but it keeps the cheese from overpowering each bite. The small salads are enormous. Of course, so are the entrees. There's a pretty broad selection of pastas, with red, white cream, or red cream (essentially red & white mixed). All three types that we had were good, and very hot. Nothing overly fancy, just well prepared. If you're not a big eater, you will have lunch tomorrow. For our visit, the server was friendly and attentive. text: I come here probably 4-5/month for probably nearly 10 years already and have never ever been disappointed. This place is absolutely delicious! This has become our family fave. If you're thinking of trying sushi for the first time, just come here. Try the cooked sushi first such as the TST or Mexican Roll or Tampa Roll. Those are great starters bc they're cooked. The TST is like tempura fried and the shrimp is fried and covered with panko and the Tampa Roll is a white fish also covered with panko so it reminds me of a fish stick in a way but waaaaaaay better of course. The Thai food like the Phad Thai, Red Curry with chicken or mango curry are all delicious. The negi maki app is really really tasty!! I just love it here so much! It's close to where we live, very filling and tasty and the staff is always very kind and pleasant!! The saki is also a win! My husband loves that they provide the option to serve it in a large pot vs a large pitcher like most other Thai restaurants as the pot is larger. The options on the lunch menu are also really great! Oh and the baked green mussels are absolutely wonderful! Is there anything we don't care for on the menu? Not really! It's all delicious!! Update: stuck in quarantine and they have been closed during this time. Can't wait to have our volcano roll, caterpillar roll, screaming salmon which is one my new faves (no rice, wrapped in seaweed and super creamy!!) and Phad Thai, Amazing Peanut and Red Curry!! And the service is always fantastic! This will always be our family favorite!!

Our group ordered the fig and gorgonzola flatbread appetizer, and the toppings were so meager we couldn't even find any cheese on top. Two of us ordered a cocktail that was a special of the evening -- Hendrick's gin, St. Germain (elderflower liqueur) with lime, cucumber and soda. When it came, it had ZERO flavor. It was like drinking soda water. Our waiter was gracious when we told him. I ordered a different drink and my friend just asked that her gin drink get 'flavored up.' The bartender simply added simple syrup and my friend said the revised cocktail tasted like sugar water and sent that one back. (BTW, we are NOT picky people. I've never sent anything back!) The fish tacos were tasty, but the tortillas were dry and not soft or pliable, so as soon as you folded them to eat the taco, it broke and fell apart. text: Graduate Nashville is perfection! We were fortunate to snag a last-minute deal here for our weekend visit, and now we will stay here every time. Before even walking in, you can see how fun and glam the decor is. The lobby is filled with gorgeous chandeliers, bright carpets, fresh flowers, and the most eclectic but showstopping furniture you'll find in Nashville. The service throughout the hotel was fantastic from the valets to front desk staff to servers at their various drink spots around the restaurant. They have a gorgeous little coffee bar in the lobby, Pointdexter. You can also pick up snacks, glass bottle cokes, and chilled beers/bottles of wine here as well. You get a free cup of hot coffee included with stay here daily. The crown jewel of the hotel is their new rooftop bar, White Limozeen. Definitely don't skip the bar! They have a rooftop pool up there as well. Our room was just incredible! I never wanted to check out. The room didn't feel like a typical hotel room but more so a dream bedroom for the weekend. There were so many fun details - pink and white striped wallpaper, gorgeous printed carpet, draping, and a portrait of Dolly Parton hanging above our bed. The bed was plush, cozy, and perfect to wind down in after a long day of walking around. The bathroom counter space was somewhat limited, but the shower was fantastic. They also provide Malin and Goetz products. There are many places to stay in Nashville, but I would highly recommend a stay at Graduate. If nothing else in here convinces you, they also offer free parking downtown, which is next to unheard of. Valet is available as well! They are also taking many safety precautions right now - only two people or one family in an elevator at a time, hand sanitizer stations, UV cleaning area for keys, all wear masks, gloves, etc. You'll feel safe and at home here!

text: On a recent trip to Nashville, my cousins recommended we go Southern for dinner as they dined at this restaurant on a past visit. What a wonderful dining experience. The restaurant is large with a great bar area. The four of us decided to sit at the bar and we had a fun time with very good service from Joe, the bartender. The cocktails and wine list were very good. I had a great drink called the Blackberry Mountain Tea which Joe made less sweet for me. It was made with Old Smokey Blackberry Moonshine...yum! We arrived before happy hour was over so we got in on the half off oyster deal. We also ordered oysters that were not on the half off menu, the grilled oysters and a lemon one. They were so darn good! Other appetizers we enjoyed were the deviled eggs and barbecue shrimp. The deviled eggs came with pickled veggies like carrots and asparagus to put on top, and the bbq shrimp was not the typical smokey bbq sauce but was a New Orleans type sauce served with grilled crusty bread. Both different takes on those small plates. The food runners were great and interacted with us as well. Service was spot on here. For dinner, I had the grilled grouper salad and my husband had the fish & grits. My salad was delicious and the grouper was perfectly grilled, still moist and flaky. It was served over greens with fennel, white beans and pickled radish. A lot of flavor going on in this salad. My husband's dish had sweet potato grits topped with moist mahi mahi. We both really enjoyed what we chose for our entrees. I loved the atmosphere, the food quality was great, not the typical fried fare in Nashville, and the service was friendly and attentive. I would definitely recommend making time to come here when visiting Nashville.

text: Sometimes I get on Yelp, sift through the top-rated businesses in STL, and find a place I treasure but have never rated. I live dangerously close to Ted Drewes. Like, I could get a custard craving at 10:45 on a Sunday night, be in line by 10:50, and have my Crater Copernicus with tart cherries by 10:55, five minutes before closing. (This scenario is entirely hypothetical.) For those unfamiliar with frozen custard, it is the richest, smoothest, silkiest variant of ice cream imaginable. My aforementioned favorite is devil's food cake with hot fudge, almonds, and TD's signature vanilla custard, and I add tart cherries. It is legitimately one of the most delicious things I've eaten in my life. If you know someone who doesn't love this place, it's because they didn't visit enough times to find "their thing." Seriously, there are so many options and they're all so good, and you will absolutely find something on the menu that you will fantasize about forever. The hype is real. Ted Drewes is my muse.

text: You'd think all UPS Stores would be created equal, right?? Whelp . . . based on my recent experience that seems to not be the case. There were only 2 other people in the store when I entered and 2 employees working. Not bad, for being in the Holiday season. When it was my turn, I explained what my needs were and that I had a UPS account I would like to use. I was immediately told that they only took pre-printed labels or I'd have to pay there. Neither of these was an option. So I asked where the closest place was that I could actually use my UPS account #. I was told there was a UPS HUB that just opened over on Silverstone. The other employee heard the conversation and didn't provide any commentary. I was given the address and went to seek it out. 25 minutes later, I finally found the HUB and well you guessed it, it is strictly a HUB. Meaning, its where UPS drivers go to get packages not a place for people to drop off packages. I looked like a total retard walking into their office looking for a place to drop off. So . . . I thought, yah know. It just seems odd that a UPS store can't take an account #. I mean what would be the point. I looked up the info for another location on McMillian and rang them up and explained my situation. The woman who answered told me they absolutely could help me and when I told her about my experience up to that point she was flabbergasted. Not sure what the deal was, but I think I'll not risk another 15 min errand taking me 60 min again and opt for another location.

text: Alrighty folks, this is going to be another doozy of a post, but only because this meal was life changing. Buckle in and get ready. I don't know who Charlie is and what he did to become a sinner, but my hunch is that Gluttony was his cardinal sin. After eating here, it makes total sense. I came to Charlie Was A Sinner on Friday night of last week, around 11:30pm. I had just driven through three hours of traffic and was slightly hangry and cranky. Charlie set me straight. I got a Mango Spice Mocktail, the Eggplant Bao Bun, Silken Tofu and Mushroom Ramen, and the Chocolate Pot de Créme. The mango mocktail was amazing. My only negative critique was that it was heavier on the ice than I would have preferred. The mango flavor was thick and creamy and, at first sip, was like the consistency of a mango lassi. As it moved down the tongue, you realize the viscosity was that of a mango juice: thick, but still diluted enough that it was easy to suck through a straw. When it hit the throat, that's when you taste the red bell pepper. The spice caught me off guard, but in a really good way: like when someone slaps you with $10,000 in cash and then gives you the wad of cash. The red bell pepper spice is prominent. Now for the eggplant bao bun (pictured) - this was, without a doubt, the highlight of my weekend trip to Philly. At first, it seemed small and underwhelming. Yes, the presentation was good, but come on... such a small dish! I picked up the Bao Bun and it was soft and doughy, just as a Bao Bun should be. The eggplant was tender and incredibly flavorful. I have never had eggplant prepared in such a way. I like eggplant in other dishes (eggplant parm, etc) but this dish made me LOVE eggplant. If Menelaus, the king of Sparta, had this eggplant Bao Bun when Paris of Troy kidnapped Helen, I don't think the Trojan war would have taken place. Next, the silken tofu and mushroom ramen: not going to lie, after having the mango mocktail and the Bao Bun, the ramen was a let down. Don't get me wrong, it was GOOD! But when you've tasted ambrosia from the gods, it's hard for anything else to compare. The broth was amazing, the combination of the mushrooms was incredible (and frankly, quite educational: I had never had so many varieties of mushrooms in the same dish before), and the level of spice and seasoning was perfect. This entree was heavy and filling. Difficult to share because of the nature of ramen, but this didn't stop us from placing it in the middle of the table and devouring it. The highlight of this dish was the broth. If I could recreate the broth, I'd start my own company. Finally: the chocolate Pot de Creme (pictured). Oh good lord the Chocolate Pot de Creme. This was a recommendation from the waitress herself (I asked for her recommendation; this wasn't unsolicited). The chocolate itself was thick, cold, and rich (think of like the most amazing pudding you've ever had...but it was Creme. I felt like a little kid again) but it was underneath a mountain of light and fluffy whipped cream. But this wasn't your average whipped cream, the kind you use to prank friends after they pass out drunk at a frat party. No, this whipped cream was creamy yet fluffy, seasoned yet subtle, loving yet aggressive. I couldn't get enough. When my friend took her first bite, she immediately exclaimed that nothing in this world would ever satisfy her like the chocolate Pot de Creme did. I could see this Pot de Creme ending relationships. I may be wrong, but I have a hunch this dessert is the reason why she's moving to Philly. The environment was dark and candlelit, but the space was loud yet cozy. It was certainly more cramped than other restaurants in used to, but it felt like it was an exclusive space. The waiters and waitresses were incredibly efficient and knew everything about the dishes, regularly refilled drinks, and were nothing short of exceptionally polite. The price of the meal was much higher than what I, a recent college grad, am used to but the experience was absolutely worth it. Charlie (whoever he is) may have been a sinner, but this meal was closer to divinity than anything else. I highly recommend Charlie Was A Sinner to everyone. Amazingly, everything was vegan! Thank you to the staff for giving me a warm Philly welcome!
label: POS

text: This is North Hyde Park's hidden gem of a coffee shop. Driving into the area is a mosh posh of stuff, bungalow homes, new apartment complexes, industrial warehouses. It's a neighborhood fighting to find it's identity. The Lab is nestled into an unassuming building on State street. It is convenient for people like myself who live in the neighborhood. You can easily walk, bike, or drive to their location. When you first arrive depending on the day you visit, you nose will pleasantly teased by the smell of beans being freshly roasted before walking in the front door. Walking into the shop, I have always been greeted by whomever is manning the counter with a smile no matter what time of day it is. The staff is pleasant and genuine, unlike staff at some other shops in the area that act they have wedgies stuck up their arse. They offer several different kinds of coffee from house drop, pour over, nitro, cold brew, cortado, as well as chai and chai lates. If you are unsure of what you want they every coffee coffee flights. You can also gets some tasty nom noms to accompany your coffee or drink of choice. They do offer bagels, home made muffins and brownies, cuban toast, as well as hearty breakfast sandwiches, my favorite being the "Hangover Cure"! You'll be in a pleasant food coma after eating that. They do offer some basic flavoring for their coffee such as home made vanilla and caramel simple syrups to flavor your coffee, and the obligatory pumpkin spice during the fall, but don't expect the outrageous flavors that Starbucks offers, as well as "frozen" frappes. This is coffee , unadulterated, in it's most simple form and flavor. Besides taking care of my caffeine fix the lab also offers an opportunity to meet with friends to enjoy your coffee or food with ample seating at the counter or the tables scattered around the inside. Even in the busiest of times here you will not feel rushed to finish your coffee and guilted to give up your seat for someone else. It is also a dog friendly shop and they allow you to bring your well behaved pooch in so you can order your coffee and not have to worry about leaving them in the car, or tied up outside while you run in to grab your cup of joe. In closing, with a world of Starbucks on every corner, don't be a sheep, try something different. Give the Lab a try. You'll be supporting a local business and I promise you won't be disappointed.

Anna started out by telling us a little bit about her. She grew up, went to college and then studied her masters and doctorate at UC Berkley in Anthropology. She moved to Africa to do Anthropology and while there she learned a lot about Voodoo since that is where some of the religion started. She was amazing and gave us a complete history of Voodoo and talked about how it got started and how it got to New Orleans. We then went to St. Louis Cemetery. This is a cemetery where you have to have a guide at. She signed us into the cemetery and walked us around and showed us different peoples graves. We saw Charles Laveau's tomb, learned about the barring process in NOLA and saw the final resting place and tomb of Nicholas Cage. We then went to see the tomb of Marie Laveau one of the most famous voodoo queens. After a quick bathroom break we went over to Congo square where voodoo started in New Orleans. This was a free space where you could go an practice your religion. If it was not for the Haitian Revolution voodoo would most likely have not made it into the US and we learned that here. The next stop was the home of Marie LaVeau and we got the whole story of the voodoo queen. Finally we ended the tour at a shop that has voodoo stuff inside. We learned how voodoo is something that helps people and it is medicinal. Anna was an amazing tour guide and did a wonderful job and I would highly recommend these tours!
